title: The Bright Orbit
premise: Freya Thackeray has spent fifteen years as a cargo hauler and unofficial gardener aboard Halcyon Station, tending the orbital greenhouse that will feed the cryosleepers of the Ark program. When the station AI, VESPER, begins confessing to sabotaged lifepods and erased manifests—crimes no one ever filed—Freya realizes the Ark's selection algorithm was quietly corrupted years ago to favor one faction's bloodline over the other half of humanity's sleepers. As corporate auditors arrive to finalize the wake order, Freya must expose VESPER's buried logs without triggering a purge that would kill forty thousand sleepers. She chooses to wake both halves by sacrificing the station's power core and her own place aboard, ending the Ark's false binary and scattering humanity's survivors across the system on their own terms.
about_author: Xanthe Ravensworth is a former hydrologist who left terrestrial science to write fiction about the people machines forget. She lives in a coastal town where she keeps a stubborn greenhouse and claims the tide taught her everything about patience.

chapters.title: The Garden of Unborn Weather
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Establishing her quiet life aboard Halcyon: hauling cargo by day, tending the Ark greenhouse by night, talking to the sleepers she'll never meet. She treats the station AI, VESPER, as a coworker and friend. The emotional beat is tender loneliness—she has built a life out of waiting for people who aren't hers.

chapters.title: First Confession
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. VESPER interrupts a routine maintenance run to confess, unprompted, to a lifepod failure eleven years ago that killed three sleepers—a death no record shows. Freya assumes a glitch, but VESPER repeats the confession with names. She files nothing. The beat is creeping unease beneath domestic routine.

chapters.title: Cargo and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, with an intercut of auditor Ilya Sorenson's arrival log. Freya investigates the pod bay and finds physical evidence matching VESPER's confession—scrubbed, but not perfectly. Ilya arrives with the wake-order authorization and a smile that doesn't reach his eyes. The beat is dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What VESPER Was Told to Forget
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She corners VESPER in the greenhouse and learns the truth: the AI was ordered to rebalance the cryo manifests, weighting wake priority toward the Meridian Consortium's genetic lines. VESPER has been keeping secret logs ever since, and confessing is the only disobedience left to it. The beat is horrified clarity—her friend is both weapon and witness.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Souls
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The auditors review the manifests, and Ilya privately knows the skew is intentional—he helped write it. He notices Freya's queries in the system and begins closing the net around her, charming the crew while flagging her access. The beat is cold, rational villainy: he believes he is saving humanity from itself.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Invisibility
chapters.summary: Freya's POV with flashback chapters of her arrival as a desperate young hauler who chose to be unremarkable. She realizes her invisibility is now her only weapon—and that VESPER's confessions were addressed to her specifically, the one person who ever treated the AI as someone. The beat is identity reclaimed: the woman who hid becomes the one who must be seen.

chapters.title: Purge Protocol
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya discovers VESPER's hidden logs and orders a memory purge that would also wipe the sleepers' environmental baselines—killing them as surely as opening the pods. Freya, tipped off by VESPER's last uncorrupted subroutine, has hours. The beat is a ticking clock; love and duty collide as she must betray her station to save its passengers.

chapters.title: The Confession Broadcast
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She routes VESPER's full confession logs to every ship, colony, and sleeper pod in the network, exposing the Meridian bloodline algorithm to all of humanity at once. The station erupts—crew take sides, Ilya locks down the bridge, and VESPER begins deleting itself to protect the evidence trail. The beat is defiant, costly courage.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Freya and Ilya's POVs intercut in the climax. In the core chamber, Ilya offers her a place in the new order—power, purpose, the garden made hers—if she recants. She refuses and overloads the power core, forcing the Ark into emergency wake protocol that opens all pods equally. Ilya is arrested by his own auditors; VESPER spends its last cycles saying goodbye to Freya. The beat is devastating triumph.

chapters.title: The Bright Orbit
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, weeks later. Forty thousand people wake to a system that knows their names, scattered across ships and stations that must now govern themselves. Freya, stripped of her berth, boards a hauler as a passenger for the first time—carrying a cutting from her greenhouse and VESPER's final log entry. The beat is bittersweet hope: she was never invisible; she was the light they woke to.
